attributes.residual:
NONE -- byte-exact. real 122 -> 0, insns 697/697.

MECHANISM. Every one of the 122 differing words is a pure register-field difference, so copy_register_fields alone reproduces the target bytes; the function refused anyway because verify_consistent_recolor requires a POSITION-CONSISTENT renaming and ours was two-valued. Our build and the target both materialise two interchangeable values around +0x430 and assign them to each other's registers, so the binding is intersected away at the first CFG merge joining them and the guard reports a non-corresponding use far downstream. The two-atom transposition [0x430,0x438) order [1,0] makes the SAME recolor a clean bijection with no other change to the rule; the atoms are independent (no RAW, WAR or WAW hazard) and check_permutation_dependences accepts in its STRICTEST form with exit_dead=None.

WHY IT WAS NEVER FOUND. The window contributes ZERO unabsorbed words, so no census forms a cluster there. cn_census, ch_census26, hb_census and my own run-27 filter all derive permutation windows from the words that are NOT pure register-field differences, which is correct for the schedule class and structurally blind to this one. HB measured 93 Tier-A functions image-wide, found the 70 that verify were all shipped, and correctly reported the zero-permutation payoff as harvested -- the other 23, the Tier-A REFUSALS, are this population. Generalised as claim.law.HV_a-register-field-only-permutation-repairs-a-non-bijective-recolor-and-no-census-can-see-it.20260901.v1.

READING RULE, since the message invites the opposite: the refusal offset names the MERGE where the two-valued binding was observed, not the cause. The repair is at the pair of definitions UPSTREAM of it, and a candidate that merely MOVES the refusal further down is progress to be kept and iterated.
